mainTopic: Disqualifying judges and witnesses through מיגו, how the חכמים treat each other, and backing out of accepting unfit judges or a lighter vow
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of the משנה where רבי מאיר lets a litigant disqualify judges and witnesses. Proving one group פסולין makes him believed about the other group too (מיגו). רבא objects that disqualifying the only witnesses would end the case. The answer is that there is another set of witnesses, and this explanation still differs from רב דימי's over whether we say מיגו. The גמרא then returns to ריש לקיש, who rereads the משנה as 'his witness' out of reverence for רבי מאיר. This leads to stories and פסוקים about how the חכמים of ארץ ישראל treat each other gently, while those of בבל argue sharply. Next come teachings about arrogance going to בבל and then עילם, and two views of the Torah of בבל. A new משנה follows: can someone who accepted unfit judges, or a vow instead of an oath, back out? רבי מאיר says yes, and the חכמים say no. The גמרא discusses which kind of offer the argument covers, and רב אחא בר תחליפא begins a challenge to רבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proving one group disqualified knocks out the other group too
steps.stepSummary: The first clause of the משנה is about a case where the witnesses were proven פסולין but the judges were not. The last clause is the reverse. In each case, once one group is proven פסולין, the other group is disqualified along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is about disqualified witnesses and fit judges: since he disqualifies the witnesses, he disqualifies the judges too. The last clause is about disqualified judges and fit witnesses: since he disqualifies the judges, he disqualifies the witnesses too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation of both clauses of the משנה. The litigant claims both the judges and the witnesses are פסולין but proves only one group, and the other group falls along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause (רישא) the litigant brings proof only against the witnesses, and that makes him believable about the judges too. In the last clause (סיפא) he proves only the judges are פסולין, and that makes him believable about the witnesses too. This explains how רבי מאיר can let him disqualify one group without bringing a separate proof for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who are not valid to testify
Judges who are fit to judge
Since; here meaning 'since one claim was proven, the other claim is believed too'
The last clause of the משנה
The first clause of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the usual מיגו ('he could have made a better claim'). Here it just means: since he proved one group is פסולין, we believe his claim about the other group too.

phrases.english: [The first clause] is about disqualified witnesses and fit judges,
since he disqualifies the witnesses,
he also disqualifies the judges.
The last clause is about disqualified judges and fit witnesses,
since he disqualifies the judges,
he also disqualifies the witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation of the משנה that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proving one group (witnesses or judges) פסולין lets the litigant disqualify the other group too, according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Disqualifying witnesses without proof would wipe out the case
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the first clause, because another court can always be found. He challenges the last clause: if the witnesses are disqualified without proof, there are no witnesses left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: It makes sense that since he disqualifies the witnesses he also disqualifies the judges, because there is another court available. But since he disqualifies the judges, can he also disqualify the witnesses? Then there are no more witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation from step 1, but only its second half, about the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the judges costs nothing permanent, since the case can go to a different בית דין. Losing the witnesses ends the case, since nobody is left to testify. רבא argues it is too much to let a litigant destroy the other side's case on a claim he never proved.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, a formula that opens a challenge
Granted / it makes sense (in the first case)

phrases.english: Rava objected to it:
Granted, since he disqualifies the witnesses
he also disqualifies the judges,
[because] there is another court.
But since he disqualifies the judges
he also disqualifies the witnesses?
But there are no more witnesses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of the explanation in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that proving the judges פסולין also disqualifies the witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Judges can be replaced by another court, but witnesses cannot. Disqualifying them without proof would end the case.

steps.title: There is another set of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה is talking about a case where the other side has a second set of witnesses, so disqualifying this set does not end the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where there is another set of witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא by limiting the case in the משנה: there is another set of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a second set of witnesses, the other side can still prove its claim, just as it can still go to another court. So knocking out one set of witnesses is no more drastic than knocking out the judges.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for, a formula that limits a teaching to a specific case

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where there is another set [of witnesses].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to one where there is another set of witnesses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to let him disqualify the only witnesses in the case, which would end it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a case with another set of witnesses, so the case can continue.

steps.title: Then this is just רב דימי's explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if there is no other set, can he really not disqualify them? If so, this explanation turns into רב דימי's explanation, which already said the משנה is about two sets of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there is no other set, what is the law? Does it mean he cannot disqualify them? Then that is the same as רב דימי's explanation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 3. Once that answer is adopted, this explanation is no longer a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 had to limit the משנה to a case with a second set of witnesses. That implies that with only one set, the litigant cannot disqualify them. But רב דימי already explained the משנה as a case of two sets of witnesses, so the new explanation adds nothing of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose explanation of the משנה (two sets of witnesses) appeared earlier

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's challenge forced this explanation to assume a second set of witnesses. Once it does, it becomes the same as רב דימי's explanation.

phrases.english: But if there is no other set, what [is the law]?
Is it really so that he cannot disqualify [them]?
That is [the same as] Rav Dimi's [explanation]!
phrases.notes: רב דימי's explanation came earlier in the סוגיא: the משנה is about two sets of witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 3 by showing what it leads to
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה is about a case with another set of witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the explanation needs two sets of witnesses, it is the same as רב דימי's and is no longer a separate explanation.

steps.title: The two explanations differ over מיגו
steps.stepSummary: The explanation from Step 3 and רב דימי's explanation are not the same. One holds that we say מיגו and the other holds that we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: מיגו. One Sage holds that we say מיגו, and the other Sage holds that we do not say מיגו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. The two explanations are not identical, because they disagree about whether we apply מיגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked whether the answer in Step 3 had simply turned into רב דימי's explanation. The גמרא says there is still a real difference. The explanation from Steps 1–3 holds that once the litigant proves one group פסולין, we believe his unproven claim about the other group (מיגו). רב דימי holds that we do not say this, so the litigant must prove every claim on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
We say, meaning we apply this rule

steps.confusionAlert: Even though both explanations talk about two sets of witnesses, they are not the same. They split over מיגו.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: מיגו,
phrases.notes: Here מיגו means: since he proved one group פסולין, we believe his claim about the other group too.

phrases.english: for one Sage holds: we say מיגו,
and one Sage holds: we do not say מיגו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4 by showing the two explanations differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a practical difference between the two explanations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Step 3 explanation seemed to collapse into רב דימי's explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over whether מיגו is applied, so both explanations stand as separate views.

steps.title: ריש לקיש changes the משנה to say one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to ריש לקיש's statement. He refuses to believe רבי מאיר would allow a litigant to disqualify the other side's witnesses, so he reads the משנה as 'his witness'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main statement. ריש לקיש said: Would a holy mouth say such a thing? Teach the משנה as 'his witness'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to look closely at ריש לקיש's statement, which was mentioned earlier. He changes the משנה's wording from 'his witnesses' to 'his witness'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש finds it impossible that רבי מאיר, the 'holy mouth', would let one side cancel the other side's witnesses. So he limits the משנה to a single witness. That case is smaller, since one witness alone cannot make the other side pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the statement itself, to discuss it in detail
A holy mouth, here meaning רבי מאיר
Teach it, meaning read the text this way

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: ריש לקיש said:
Would a holy mouth say this thing?
phrases.notes: The 'holy mouth' is רבי מאיר, whose view is in the משנה.

phrases.english: Teach: 'his witness'.
phrases.notes: The משנה says עֵדָיו, 'his witnesses'. ריש לקיש reads it as one witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מיגו discussion and returns to ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה should be read as 'his witness', one witness, because רבי מאיר would not let a litigant disqualify the other side's witnesses.

steps.title: Was ריש לקיש really so humble?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions ריש לקיש's humble tone. עולא described ריש לקיש as so sharp that he seemed to uproot mountains and grind them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But עולא said: Whoever sees ריש לקיש in the בית המדרש, it is as if he uproots mountains and grinds them against each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's humble words, 'a holy mouth'. A scholar as sharp as ריש לקיש would be expected to argue strongly, not hold back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about attitude, not halacha. According to עולא, ריש לקיש was a powerful thinker who took on any argument. So why would he treat רבי מאיר's words as too holy to question?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It opens a challenge
Uprooting mountains: a picture of brilliant, powerful reasoning

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't עולא say:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה אֶת רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: One who sees ריש לקיש in the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ עוֹקֵר הָרִים וְטוֹחֲנָן זֶה בָּזֶה.
phrases.english: it is as though he uproots mountains and grinds them into each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the humble tone of ריש לקיש's statement in Step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A scholar as sharp as ריש לקיש would not simply defer to someone else's words.

steps.title: רבי מאיר was even greater
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רבי מאיר was even greater than ריש לקיש. Whoever saw him seemed to see someone uprooting the very biggest mountains, so ריש לקיש was right to speak of him with awe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: But isn't it true that whoever sees רבי מאיר in the בית המדרש, it is as if he uproots the highest mountains and grinds them against each other!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. ריש לקיש was great, but רבי מאיר was greater, so respect was fitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא uses the same mountain picture but makes it bigger: 'mountains of mountains'. ריש לקיש was sharp, but he was speaking about someone on an even higher level. So his humble words make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Mountains of mountains: the very greatest mountains

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש reads the משנה as 'his witness', one witness, out of respect for רבי מאיר. That respect fits, because רבי מאיר was even greater than the very sharp ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: רבינא said:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל הָרוֹאֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: But isn't it so that anyone who sees רבי מאיר in the study hall,
it is as though he uproots the highest of mountains
and grinds them into each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל הָרוֹאֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Compares the two scholars: רבי מאיר was greater
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ריש לקיש was so sharp, his humble tone seemed out of character.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר was greater still, so ריש לקיש rightly spoke of him with awe.

steps.title: The question was really praise for how the scholars love each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that its earlier question about ריש לקיש's humble tone was not a real challenge. It was a way of saying: see how much the חכמים love each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the גמרא meant: come and see how much the scholars love one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its question in Step 7 and changes how we should read it. It was never an attack; it was an expression of admiration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 it sounded like the גמרא was asking, 'How could someone as sharp as ריש לקיש speak so humbly?' Now the גמרא says the question was really pointing at something beautiful. Even a giant like ריש לקיש spoke about רבי מאיר with deep respect.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the earlier words should be understood this way)
Come and see (a phrase that points to something worth noticing)
They love and cherish one another

steps.confusionAlert: Step 8 already gave an answer through רבינא. This line adds a different angle: the question itself was never really a question. It was praise.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Come and see
how much they love one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes how we read the question in Step 7. It turns out to be praise, not a challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גמרא was challenging ריש לקיש's humble way of speaking about רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא was not challenging anything. It was admiring the love and respect between the חכמים.

steps.title: רבי gives way to the ruling of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the same respect. רבי forbade wrapping cold food on שבת. When רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי told him that his father allowed it, רבי accepted the elder's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the time רבי was sitting and teaching that it is forbidden to wrap up cold food on שבת. רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי told him, 'My father allowed wrapping cold food.' רבי then told the people: 'The elder has already ruled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as another example of how the חכמים respected each other. רבי changes his own ruling out of respect for רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was the leader of the generation, and he had already stated his own view. Even so, as soon as he heard that the older sage רבי יוסי had ruled otherwise, he followed him. The point is the respect he showed, not the details of the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: To wrap or cover food so it keeps its temperature
The elder (an older, earlier sage) has already given a ruling

phrases.english: Like that time when Rabbi was sitting and saying:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: It is forbidden to wrap up cold food (on Shabbos).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
My father permitted wrapping up cold food.
He said to them: The elder has already ruled.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי, and 'the elder' is רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that shows the same love between חכמים described in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים love and respect one another
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי accepting רבי יוסי's ruling about wrapping cold food

steps.title: רב פפא explains why the story is so striking
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that רבי יוסי, if he had been alive, would have been like a student of רבי. His son, who was just as great, actually sat as רבי's student. Yet רבי still gave way to רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Come and see how much they loved each other. If רבי יוסי had been alive, he would have sat humbly before רבי as a student. We know this because his son רבי ישמעאל, who was as great as his fathers, did sit humbly before רבי. And still רבי said, 'The elder has already ruled.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the lesson of the story we just heard. He shows that רבי was humbling himself before someone who would have ranked below him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think רבי followed רבי יוסי because רבי יוסי was the greater sage. רב פפא says no: his son, who was just as great, was רבי's student, so רבי יוסי would have been too. That makes רבי's respect even more impressive.

keyTerms.meaning: Bowed and sitting (humbly, as a student before his teacher)
Filling the place of his fathers (equal in greatness to them)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that showing respect to another sage is not only about who ranks higher. Even a leader gives honor to the ruling of an older sage.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה מְחַבְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: Come and see how much they love one another,
for if Rabbi Yosei had been alive,
he would have been bowed and sitting before Rabbi.
For Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
was filling the place of his fathers,
and he was bowed and sitting before Rabbi,
and yet he said: The elder has already ruled.
phrases.notes: The one speaking here is רבי himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה מְחַבְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the lesson of the story in Step 10 and why it is so striking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי showed great respect by following the ruling of רבי יוסי, even though רבי יוסי would have been his student.

steps.title: Pleasantness and Binders: the scholars of ארץ ישראל and בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא reads the two staffs in זכריה as two styles of learning. The scholars of ארץ ישראל are gentle with each other in הלכה, while the scholars of בבל are sharp with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: What does the פסוק mean when it says, 'I took two staffs; one I called Pleasantness and one I called Binders'? 'Pleasantness' is the תלמידי חכמים of ארץ ישראל, who are pleasant to each other when they discuss הלכה. 'Binders' is the תלמידי חכמים of בבל, who hurt each other when they discuss הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that sums up the stories it just told. The kind respect we saw from ריש לקיש and רבי is the style of the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא uses a play on words: חוֹבְלִים ('binders') sounds like מְחַבְּלִים ('hurting'). Both ריש לקיש and רבי were sages of ארץ ישראל, so their gentleness fits the 'Pleasantness' staff. The scholars of בבל argue more sharply with each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Being pleasant and gentle to one another

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches that great sages, even when they disagree, should treat each other with love and respect. Examples: ריש לקיש's awe of רבי מאיר, and רבי giving way to רבי יוסי. רבי אושעיא calls this the 'Pleasantness' of the scholars of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
What is meant by that which is written:
"And I took for myself two staffs;
phrases.notes: זכריה 11:7

phrases.english: one I called Pleasantness,
and the other I called Binders"?
"Pleasantness": these are the Torah scholars in the Land of Israel,
who are pleasant to one another in halacha.
"Binders": these are the Torah scholars in Babylonia,
who hurt one another in halacha.
phrases.notes: A play on words: חובלים sounds like מחבלים, 'hurting'. He means they speak sharply to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the stories about respect to a פסוק and contrasts ארץ ישראל with בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scholars of ארץ ישראל are gentle with each other in הלכה, while the scholars of בבל are sharp with each other.

steps.title: Oil and olives: gentle scholars and sharp scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads the 'sons of oil' in זכריה as the scholars of ארץ ישראל, who are smooth with each other like olive oil. He reads the 'two olive trees' as the scholars of בבל, who are bitter with each other like a raw olive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'These are the two sons of oil who stand…' and 'two olive trees beside it.' רבי יצחק says: the 'oil' means the scholars of ארץ ישראל, who are pleasant to each other in הלכה like olive oil. The 'two olive trees' means the scholars of בבל, who are bitter to each other in הלכה like an olive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second reading from the same vision in זכריה. It makes the same point as רבי אושעיא's two staffs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil and olives come from the same fruit, but they taste very different. Oil is smooth, and a raw olive is bitter. In the same way, both groups learn the same תורה, but ארץ ישראל scholars argue gently and בבל scholars argue sharply.

keyTerms.meaning: Pleasant and easy with one another
Bitter and sharp with one another

phrases.english: "Then he said to me: These are the [two] anointed ones,
phrases.notes: זכריה 4:14. The word in square brackets isn't in every version. Literally the פסוק says 'sons of oil.'

phrases.english: that stand, etc."
"And two olive trees by it."
phrases.notes: זכריה 4:3, a different פסוק from the same vision.

phrases.english: "Oil": Rabbi Yitzchak says:
These are the Torah scholars in Eretz Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנּוֹחִין זֶה לָזֶה בַּהֲלָכָה כְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת.
phrases.english: who are pleasant to each other in halakha like olive oil.
"And two olive trees by it":
these are the Torah scholars in Babylonia,
who are bitter to each other in halakha like an olive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel reading of a פסוק that backs up רבי אושעיא's contrast between ארץ ישראל and בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil stands for the gentle scholars of ארץ ישראל, and olives stand for the sharp scholars of בבל

steps.title: The women carrying the measure to שנער
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, explains the vision of two women carrying an איפה to the land of שנער. It shows flattery and arrogance going down to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: זכריה saw two women with wings like a stork's, carrying a measure between heaven and earth. He asked the angel where they were taking it. The angel said: 'To build a house for it in the land of שנער.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: this is flattery and arrogance, which went down to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads another vision in זכריה. It says the thing carried in the measure is flattery and arrogance, and they were brought to בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שנער is another name for the area of בבל. So the angel's answer, 'to build it a house in שנער,' means these bad traits were taken to בבל. This new claim sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The land of שנער, the area of בבל

phrases.english: "Then I lifted my eyes and saw,
phrases.notes: זכריה 5:9–11

phrases.english: and behold, two women came out,
and wind was in their wings,
and they had wings like the wings of a stork,
and they lifted up the measure
between the heaven and the earth.
Then I said to the angel that spoke with me:
To where are they taking the measure?
And he said to me:
To build her a house in the land of Shinar."
phrases.notes: שנער is the old name for the region of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
This is flattery and arrogance
that went down to Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another vision in זכריה that also speaks about בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure carried to שנער is flattery and arrogance going down to בבל

steps.title: Didn't arrogance go mostly to עילם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that arrogance went down to בבל. A known teaching says nine of the ten portions of arrogance went to עילם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did arrogance really go down to בבל? But a חכם taught: ten measures of arrogance came down to the world. עילם took nine, and the whole rest of the world took only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's reading. Another teaching says arrogance landed mainly in עילם, not in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If almost all arrogance went to עילם, how can the פסוק say it went to בבל? The two teachings seem to point to different places.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say? (bringing a teaching to challenge)

phrases.english: And did arrogance go down to Babylonia?
But doesn't the Master say:
Ten kav of arrogance came down to the world;
Eilam took nine,
and the whole rest of the world took one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגַסּוּת הָרוּחַ לְבָבֶל נְחִית? וְהָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that arrogance went down to בבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching says nine of ten measures of arrogance went to עילם, so it did not settle in בבל

steps.title: It came to בבל but moved on to עילם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that arrogance did go down to בבל, but it did not stay there. It slipped over to עילם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it went down to בבל, but it slipped over and spread on to עילם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both teachings are true, because arrogance arrived in בבל first and then moved on to עילם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל was only a stop along the way. עילם is where arrogance ended up and stayed, so the two teachings do not really disagree.

phrases.english: Yes, it went down to Babylonia,
but it slipped over to Eilam.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it stretched itself over.' It passed through בבל and moved on. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciling the two teachings: one describes where it arrived, the other where it stayed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings name different places for arrogance, so they contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Arrogance arrived in בבל but moved on and settled in עילם

steps.title: The wording 'to build her a house' supports this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the פסוק's own wording fits the answer. It says the women went 'to build' a house in שנער, which describes a plan, not that the house was built for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, because it says: 'To build her a house in the land of שנער.' Learn from this that arrogance did not stay in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the words of the פסוק and closes the discussion with 'שמע מינה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'to build,' which only tells us the purpose of the trip. It does not say the house was actually built and lived in. That fits the answer that arrogance came to בבל but did not stay there.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (support from the text)
Learn from it, conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: Arrogance went down to בבל but did not stay. It moved on to עילם, and the פסוק's word 'to build' hints that it never settled in בבל.

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
as it is written: "To build her a house in the land of Shinar."
phrases.notes: 'To build' tells us only what they planned. It does not say the house was actually built there.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 16 from the wording of the פסוק
steps.raayaObject: The answer that arrogance passed through בבל but did not stay
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'לבנות' in זכריה 5:11, which describes a plan to build rather than a finished house

steps.title: Poverty went to בבל, so arrogance should be there too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer that arrogance did not stay in בבל. A known teaching says poverty is a sign of arrogance, and poverty went down to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Master taught that poverty is a sign of arrogance, and poverty went down to בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the answer that arrogance slipped away from בבל to עילם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If poverty is a sign of arrogance, then where poverty is, arrogance is too. Since poverty went down to בבל, arrogance should have stayed in בבל. That clashes with the answer in step 16 that it moved on to עילם.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say? An opening that brings a known teaching as a challenge

phrases.english: But doesn't the Master say:
A sign of arrogance is poverty,
and poverty went down to Babylonia!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from steps 16-17 that arrogance did not stay in בבל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that arrogance left בבל and settled in עילם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Poverty goes together with arrogance, and poverty is in בבל, so arrogance must be in בבל as well.

steps.title: The poverty meant is poverty in Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the poverty linked to arrogance is poverty in Torah, not poverty in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What poverty is meant? Poverty in Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining which kind of poverty the teaching means. The proof that this is עילם comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge took 'poverty' to mean being poor in money, which is what went to בבל. The answer says the poverty that goes with arrogance is being poor in Torah. That kind of poverty is not in בבל, so the challenge falls away.

phrases.english: What poverty is meant?
Poverty of Torah,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by narrowing what 'poverty' means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: the poverty is in Torah, not in money.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Poverty means lack of money, which is found in בבל, so arrogance would be there too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The poverty tied to arrogance is poverty in Torah, which is not what בבל has.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that עילם is the place poor in Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק, explained by רבי יוחנן, showing that עילם is the place poor in Torah. Its people learned but could not teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts.' רבי יוחנן said: This is עילם, which was able to learn but not able to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a פסוק showing that Torah-poverty belongs to עילם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sister with 'no breasts' cannot nurse others. רבי יוחנן reads this as עילם: they learned Torah themselves but did not produce people who could teach it. So the Torah-poverty, and the arrogance that goes with it, fits עילם and not בבל.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״אָחוֹת לָנוּ קְטַנָּה וְשָׁדַיִם אֵין לָהּ״.
phrases.english: As it is written: 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 8:8

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: This is Eilam,
which merited to learn but did not merit to teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: אָחוֹת לָנוּ קְטַנָּה וְשָׁדַיִם אֵין לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 19 by showing that the Torah-poor place is עילם.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the poverty linked to arrogance is Torah-poverty, found in עילם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 8:8 as explained by רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Arrogance went down to בבל but settled in עילם. Its sign, poverty in Torah, also belongs to עילם, a place that learned but did not teach.

steps.title: The name בבל means 'mixed' with all parts of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the name בבל as praise: it is 'mixed' with מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the name בבל mean? רבי יוחנן said: It is mixed with Scripture, mixed with משנה, and mixed with תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has said בבל is not poor in Torah, it brings a saying that praises the Torah of בבל through its name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the name בבל as coming from בלולה, 'mixed'. In בבל, every level of Torah learning is blended together and fully present. This fits the earlier point that Torah-poverty is not in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The study and explanation of the משנה

phrases.english: What is the meaning of Babylonia? Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Mixed with Scripture, mixed with Mishna,
phrases.notes: He's playing on the sound: בבל sounds like בלולה, 'mixed'.

phrases.english: mixed with Talmud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from עילם's weakness in Torah to praise of בבל's Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name בבל shows it is full of all levels of Torah learning.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה calls the Talmud of בבל 'dark places'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה reads a פסוק in איכה about sitting in dark places as referring to the Talmud of בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He has made me sit in dark places, like those long dead.' רבי ירמיה said: This is the Talmud of בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second view of the Torah of בבל, which sounds much less flattering than רבי יוחנן's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן praised בבל's Torah as full and complete. רבי ירמיה instead links the Talmud of בבל to 'dark places', a picture of learning that is hard to see through. The two sayings stand side by side as different views.

phrases.english: 'He has made me dwell in dark places, like those long dead':
phrases.notes: איכה 3:6

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
This is the Talmud of Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting, less flattering view of בבל's Torah after רבי יוחנן's praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Talmud of בבל is compared to dark places.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of בבל's Torah: רבי יוחנן sees it as full and blended, and רבי ירמיה sees it as dark.

steps.title: משנה: Accepting unqualified judges, can he back out?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: one side in a case agrees to let his father, the other side's father, or three cattle herders judge. רבי מאיר says he can take it back, and the חכמים say he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one side says to the other: 'My father is trusted by me,' 'Your father is trusted by me,' or 'Three cattle herders are trusted by me,' רבי מאיר says he can take it back, and the חכמים say he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether someone who agreed to be judged by people who are normally not allowed to judge can change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fathers are relatives, and cattle herders do not know the law, so normally none of them can serve as judges. Here one side chose to accept them anyway. רבי מאיר says that agreement is not binding, so he can back out. The חכמים say his agreement holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Is trusted by me, I accept him
To go back on his word, to retract

steps.confusionAlert: 'He can retract' is about the person who made the offer. It is not about the judges.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he said to him:
'My father is trusted by me,'
phrases.notes: He means: I accept my father as judge in our case.

phrases.english: 'Your father is trusted by me,'
'Three cattle herders are trusted by me.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: He can retract,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: He cannot retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר לוֹ: נֶאֱמָן עָלַי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the aggadic discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: he who accepted unqualified judges may retract. חכמים: he may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question for the coming גמרא: how binding is an agreement to accept judges who are normally not allowed?

steps.title: משנה: Accepting a vow instead of an oath, can he back out?
steps.stepSummary: Second case: someone owed a שבועה is told, 'Just vow to me by the life of your head.' Again רבי מאיר says the one who offered can take it back, and the חכמים say he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone owed his fellow an oath, and the fellow said, 'Vow to me by the life of your head,' רבי מאיר says he can take it back, and the חכמים say he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second, parallel case with the same disagreement, this time about swapping a real oath for a lighter vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the person owed a full שבועה. The other side let him off with a weaker promise, 'by the life of your head'. רבי מאיר lets the one who offered go back and demand the full שבועה. The חכמים hold him to his offer.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath required by the court
By the life of your head, a lighter form of promise

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases of this משנה, one side gives up something he is owed: proper judges, or a full שבועה. רבי מאיר lets him back out, and the חכמים do not.

phrases.english: If one was obligated to take an oath to his fellow,
and he said to him: 'Vow to me by the life of your head,'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: He can retract,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: He cannot retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second case in the same משנה with the same disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: one who accepted a vow in place of an oath may retract. חכמים: he may not.

steps.title: The relative was accepted as one of three judges
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the משנה is talking about someone who accepted his father or the other side's father as one judge on a court of three. It is not talking about accepting him as the only judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב דימי, son of רב נחמן, son of רב יוסף, said: The case is where he accepted him as one of the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the new משנה. It clarifies what kind of acceptance of a relative the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a person agreed to let his father or the other side's father judge. רב דימי says this means the relative sits as one judge among three, and the other two judges are fit. So the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
For example; such as the case where
He accepted him upon himself (agreed to him as judge)

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: Rav Dimi, son of Rav Nachman, said,
son of Rav Yosef:
For example, where he accepted him upon himself as one.
phrases.notes: "One" means one of the three judges on the court. The other two are regular, fit judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from steps 23-24 by defining the case of accepting a relative.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The relative in the משנה was accepted as one of three judges, not as the only judge.

steps.title: שמואל: the argument is only about "it is forgiven to you"
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue when the claimant says, "The money is forgiven to you." When the defendant says, "I will give you," everyone agrees he can take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The argument is about "it is forgiven to you." But about "I will give you," everyone agrees he can take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל limits the argument in the משנה to one kind of offer, "it is forgiven to you."
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of offers. In "it is forgiven to you," the claimant agrees to give up his claim if the relative rules that way. In "I will give you," the defendant agrees to pay if the relative rules that way. שמואל says only the first is argued about. In the second, even the חכמים agree that the defendant can back out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forgiven to you (the claimant gives up his claim)
I will give you (the defendant agrees to pay)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two sides straight. "It is forgiven to you" is said by the one claiming money. "I will give you" is said by the one being sued.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The argument is about "it is forgiven to you,"
phrases.notes: This is the claimant saying: if this judge rules against me, I forgive the money.

phrases.english: but about "I will give you"
everyone agrees he can take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the משנה's case. Now it asks which kind of offer the argument covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about "it is forgiven to you." With "I will give you," everyone agrees the offer can be taken back.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the argument is about "I will give you"
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with שמואל. He says the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is about "I will give you."
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The argument is about "I will give you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different view of which offer the משנה's argument is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, everyone agrees about "I will give you." For רבי יוחנן, it is exactly there that רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue. That means the חכמים hold that even the defendant cannot take back "I will give you." רבי יוחנן does not say what happens with "it is forgiven to you," and that sets up the next question.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
About "I will give you" there is an argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with שמואל's view in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument in the משנה is about "I will give you."

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן hold about "it is forgiven to you"?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask about רבי יוחנן's view. Maybe the argument is only about "I will give you," and everyone agrees that "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back. Or maybe both cases are argued about.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the argument about "I will give you," while about "it is forgiven to you" everyone agrees he cannot take it back? Or perhaps the argument is about both?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about רבי יוחנן's opinion. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן only said that "I will give you" is argued about. There are two ways to read him. One way: "it is forgiven to you" is an easy case where everyone agrees the offer stands. The other way: רבי מאיר disagrees there too, so both cases are argued about.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Both in this case and in that case

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Is the argument about "I will give you,"
but about "it is forgiven to you"

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ?
phrases.english: everyone agrees he cannot take it back?
Or perhaps
in both this and that there is an argument?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי יוחנן's view from step 27 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In רבי יוחנן's view, does everyone agree that "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back, or is that case also argued about?

steps.title: רבא: "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back, by everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבא's statement. The argument is about "I will give you." With "it is forgiven to you," everyone agrees the offer cannot be taken back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבא said: The argument is about "I will give you." But about "it is forgiven to you," everyone agrees he cannot take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 28 with a statement of רבא. Step 30 explains how it proves the point, and step 31 rejects the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's statement matches the first possibility in the question. Only "I will give you" is argued about, and in "it is forgiven to you" even רבי מאיר agrees the claimant cannot back out. The גמרא will try to use this to show what רבי יוחנן holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source that answers the question)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. שמואל: the argument is about "it is forgiven to you," and everyone agrees "I will give you" can be taken back. רבי יוחנן: the argument is about "I will give you." רבא: the argument is about "I will give you," and everyone agrees "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rava said:
The argument is about "I will give you,"
but about "it is forgiven to you"

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees he cannot take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only "I will give you" is argued about. With "it is forgiven to you," everyone agrees the offer cannot be taken back.

steps.title: How רבא's statement shows what רבי יוחנן meant
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן holds the argument is only about "I will give you," then רבא matches רבי יוחנן. If רבי יוחנן holds both cases are argued about, רבא would match nobody.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say the argument is only about "I will give you," and everyone agrees "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back. Then רבא is following רבי יוחנן. But if you say both cases are argued about, whose view is רבא following?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's statement from the last step answers the question about רבי יוחנן. רבא only fits with someone if רבי יוחנן limits the argument to "I will give you."
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the argument is about "it is forgiven to you," and רבא clearly disagrees with that. So רבא must be following רבי יוחנן, and that only works if רבי יוחנן agrees that "it is forgiven to you" can never be taken back. Otherwise רבא would match neither שמואל nor רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say (this works well if we explain it this way)
Like whom? (whose opinion is this following?)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that with "I will give you" there is a dispute,
but with "it is forgiven to you"

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ,
phrases.english: everyone agrees he cannot take it back,
then רבא is saying it like רבי יוחנן.
But if you say
that in both this case and that case there is a dispute,
then whose view is רבא following?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the proof from רבא given in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יוחנן, everyone agrees "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement that "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back by anyone's view. That statement must follow someone, and it can only follow רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Maybe רבא was giving his own opinion
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רבא may have been stating his own understanding, not following רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא is saying his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. רבא does not have to be following anyone, because he can explain the argument his own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that רבא must agree with either שמואל or רבי יוחנן. But an אמורא like רבא can have his own reading of the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים. So his words tell us nothing about what רבי יוחנן holds, and the question from step 28 stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבא's ruling is wrong. It only means we can't use it to figure out רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: רבא is saying his own reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the use of רבא as evidence for רבי יוחנן's view. It does not reject רבא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed רבא must be following either שמואל or רבי יוחנן, when he could hold his own view.

steps.title: רב אחא בר תחליפא challenges רבא from the oath case
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר תחליפא quotes the משנה. If someone owes his friend an oath and the friend says, "Vow to me by the life of your head," רבי מאיר says the friend can take it back, and the חכמים say he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר תחליפא challenged רבא: If a person owed his friend an oath, and the friend said to him, "Vow to me by the life of your head," רבי מאיר says he can take it back, and the חכמים say he cannot take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר תחליפא begins an attack on רבא by quoting the next case in the משנה. This step sets up the challenge, and the גמרא will spell out the point next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person who is owed an oath gives up the real oath and accepts a weaker vow instead. That looks like giving something up, much like "it is forgiven to you," and still רבי מאיר says he can take it back. This seems to go against רבא's claim that everyone agrees a giving-up offer cannot be taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a משנה or ברייתא)
An oath (here, one required by Torah law)
By the life of your head (a weaker vow, not a real oath)
To take it back (back out of the offer)

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא בר תחליפא challenged רבא:
If a person owed his friend an oath,
and the friend said to him, "Vow to me by the life of your head,"

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ,
phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: he can take it back,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and the חכמים say: he cannot take it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question about רבי יוחנן and starts a direct challenge against רבא's ruling, using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that everyone agrees "it is forgiven to you" cannot be taken back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the oath case, the person owed the oath gives up his right, which looks like "it is forgiven to you." Yet רבי מאיר says he can take it back, so not everyone agrees. The full point is spelled out in the next lines.
